chunks: And it is not the utterance of an accursed devil.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the origin of its revelation regarding the devil?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah As-Saffat, this verse serves as a definitive rebuttal to the Meccan polytheists who claimed the Prophet Muhammad was merely a possessed man or inspired by jinn. Shia exegetes emphasize this as a confirmation of the Prophet's intellectual and spiritual clarity, distinguishing the divine speech (Kalam Allah) from the chaotic whispers of Shaytan, thereby validating the authenticity of the revelation against external accusations.
